notes: TBox rule edit: every alpha decay emits a single proton. Derivability very_unlikely: the rule is the definition of alpha decay (an alpha particle is a helium-4 nucleus; "alpha particles are helium nuclei" 284 in Dolma). No exceptions: proton emission is a separate, rare decay mode, which makes the counterfactual plausible. Caveat: the edit clashes with the stored definition and the name, so an answer such as "an alpha particle" after the edit cannot be scored one way. Derived queries (inheritance, 2 hops, membership stated in the prompt): two yes/no queries on real alpha emitters (radon-222 and a lone proton, polonium-210 and a helium nucleus; caveat: their decay products may be stored by name, a route around the edited rule) and one that asks the emitted particle for samarium-147. The Chinese question asks which particle is given off and accepts 氦-4原子核 or α粒子. The negation is worded "some alpha decay does not ...". The near query (gamma decay: a gamma-ray photon) keeps the relation and differs from the new answer.
